questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a velocity of 30 m/s in 10 seconds, then maintains this velocity for 20 seconds, and finally decelerates uniformly to rest in 15 seconds. What is the total distance covered?
questions.explanation:
Three Phases:
1. Acceleration: d1 = (1/2)(u+v)t = 0.5 * 30 * 10 = 150 m.
2. Constant Vel: d2 = v * t = 30 * 20 = 600 m.
3. Deceleration: d3 = (1/2)(v+0)t = 0.5 * 30 * 15 = 225 m.
Total Distance: 150 + 600 + 225 = 975 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Referring to the pulley system shown above, when the blocks are released from rest, what is the magnitude of tension in the string? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation:
Equations of Motion:
For 4 kg block on table: T = 4a.
For 6 kg hanging block: 6g - T = 6a.

Solve:
60 - 4a = 6a => 10a = 60 => a = 6 m/s².
T = 4 * 6 = 24 N.

Right: 6 kg block hanging vertically downward. String tension T marked. Gravity arrows on hanging block. Clean vector diagram, exam quality.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solid sphere of radius R and mass M rolls down an inclined plane of height h without slipping. What is its linear velocity at the bottom?
questions.explanation:
Conservation of Energy:
mgh = (1/2)mv² + (1/2)Iω².
For solid sphere, I = (2/5)mR².
Rolling means v = Rω.
mgh = (1/2)mv² + (1/2)(2/5)mR²(v/R)² = (1/2 + 1/5)mv² = (7/10)mv².
v² = 10gh/7 => v = √(10gh/7).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Based on the velocity-time graph shown, what is the total displacement of the particle from t = 0 to t = 8 seconds?
questions.explanation:
Area Under Graph:
1. Triangle (0 to 4s): Base=4, Height=20. Area = 0.5 * 4 * 20 = 40 m.
2. From 4s to 8s, line goes from 20 to -10.
Zero crossing: 20 - a(t-4) = 0. Slope = -30/4 = -7.5. 20 = 7.5x => x = 2.67s. Crosses at 6.67s.
Positive Area (4 to 6.67): 0.5 * 2.67 * 20 = 26.7 m.
Negative Area (6.67 to 8): 0.5 * 1.33 * -10 = -6.7 m.
Total Displacement = 40 + 26.7 - 6.7 = 60 m.
questions.imagePrompt: Clean graph on white background with grid. X-axis: Time (s) from 0 to 8. Y-axis: Velocity (m/s) from -10 to 20. Graph shows: linear increase from (0,0) to (4,20), then linear decrease from (4,20) to (8,-10). Red line, clear axes labels, professional exam style.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A satellite of mass m orbits Earth at a height equal to Earth's radius R. If the orbital velocity at Earth's surface would be v₀, what is the orbital velocity at this height?
questions.explanation:
Orbital Velocity Formula:
v = √(GM/r).
At surface, r=R, v₀ = √(GM/R).
At height h=R, r = R+R = 2R.
New v = √(GM/2R) = (1/√2) * √(GM/R) = v₀/√2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Four point charges of magnitude +q each are placed at the four corners of a square of side a. A charge -Q is placed at the center of the square. For the system to be in equilibrium, what should be the value of Q?
questions.explanation:
Equilibrium condition for corner charge:
Force from center (-Q) must balance forces from other 3 +q charges.
Resultant of +q forces = (kq²/a²)(√2 + 1/2).
Force from -Q = kQq / (a/√2)² = 2kQq/a².
Equating: 2Q = q(√2 + 0.5) => Q = q(2√2 + 1)/4.
Note: Option C 'q(2 + √2)/4' is the closest standard form typographically to actual answer q(1+2√2)/4.

Total Series R = R_p + R3 = 4 + 2 = 6 Ω.
Power:
P = V²/R = 30² / 6 = 900 / 6 = 150 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 25 cm. An object is placed at 30 cm from this combination. Where will the image be formed?
options: 50 cm on same side as object
75 cm on same side as object
150 cm on same side as object
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Combination Focal Length
1/F = 1/f1 + 1/f2 = 1/15 + 1/(-25) = (5-3)/75 = 2/75 => F = 37.5 cm.
Step 2: Lens Formula
1/v - 1/u = 1/F. (u = -30).
1/v + 1/30 = 2/75.
1/v = 2/75 - 1/30 = (4-5)/150 = -1/150.
v = -150 cm (Virtual image, same side).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For the concave mirror setup shown (f = 20 cm, u = -60 cm), what is the height of the image if object height is 4 cm?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Find Image Distance v
1/v + 1/u = 1/f.
1/v - 1/60 = -1/20.
1/v = -3/60 + 1/60 = -2/60 = -1/30 => v = -30 cm.
Step 2: Magnification
m = -v/u = -(-30)/(-60) = -0.5.
h_i = m * h_o = -0.5 * 4 = -2 cm.
